questions.title: How do we bring in Wordcraft?
questions.context: Wordcraft (github.com/storytold/wordcraft) is an MIT/Apache, open-source Rust reimplementation of Word. It runs in the browser through WebAssembly, has tracked changes and comments, and agents drive it through an MCP server with 422 commands. It is alpha: 634 open issues, no real-time co-editing. AIA's report is built from a document model whose every number is a ledger reference, then rendered to DOCX, so an outside editor has to keep those references intact.
questions.example: Under (a), a one-week evaluation chunk loads a real fictional AIA report into Wordcraft in the browser, has the Lead propose a tracked change through its MCP server, and checks that the numbers survive a round trip. Then you choose (b) or (c) on what it shows.

options.label: Evaluate first, then decide
options.detail: One spike chunk in W1: embed, Lead edits via MCP, ledger references survive; a go/no-go for you

options.label: Adopt it as the MVP editor now
options.detail: Context file and reports edited in Wordcraft; the alpha risk sits on the critical path

options.label: Build our own suggestions UI
options.detail: Tracked changes inside AIA's current editor; Wordcraft stays a reference

questions.rationale: It's alpha, and our numbers must stay ledger references. A short test answers whether it fits before the MVP depends on it, and Q13's editing rule holds whichever editor wins.

questions.title: May Brave receive queries written from a client's design?
questions.context: Your Q16 note: Brave for all queries, not just Class C. Brave runs outside the EU, and today it may only receive public-context (Class C) queries. A query written from a study's design is Class B by rule (ADR 0008). Allowing it means approving a non-EU route for Class B, the way you approved panel data for Bedrock EU (OI-61), and it would be recorded the same way. Class A (a client's own sources and approved knowledge) would still never go.
questions.example: A design asks how Czech 18-25s see energy-drink prices. Today the Lead may only search 'ceny energetických nápojů ČR 2026'. Under (a), it may also send 'energy drinks price perception 18-25 Czech students', which is written from the design, to Brave, for an OPEN client. A CLASSIFIED client still gets no search.

options.label: Class B to Brave, OPEN clients only
options.detail: Recorded as your determination; never Class A; CLASSIFIED clients excluded

options.label: Class B to Brave for every client
Keep Brave at Class C
options.detail: Class B waits for an EU provider

questions.rationale: It gives the search quality you want where clients allow it. CLASSIFIED clients and their sources stay protected, and the decision is on record for an audit.

questions.title: Do I keep merging the PRs I've reviewed?
questions.context: Your mandate says I merge any green PR I've reviewed. After I merged #524 at 20:29, the session's automatic permission check blocked my next message as 'Merge Without Review': it doesn't count my own review. Next up: #525 (green now), then #516 → #522 → #523 and the evidence PRs once you sign MP16.
questions.example: Under (a), you add allow rules for this session (the GitHub merge tool and session messages), and #525 merges itself at 21:45, once develop's CI is free. Under (b), you type 'merge #525' here, and I merge it then.

options.label: Keep merging; I'll add the allow rule
options.detail: Rules for mcp__github__merge_pull_request and mcp__claude-code-remote__send_message in this session's permissions

options.label: I approve each merge
options.detail: You type 'merge #N' here; I merge only then

questions.rationale: Every merge is still reviewed, green and pinned to an exact commit. (b) puts you on the critical path for about twelve merges this week.
